newsitem.title: USA: Possible suspect caught in "British bandits" case.
newsitem.headline: Possible suspect caught in "British bandits" case.

text.p: Police launched an intense manhunt in one of Washington's lushest suburbs for a possible member of a gang nicknamed the "British bandits" after they captured a second suspect during a dramatic chase on Tuesday.
Police used bloodhounds and helicopters to search the heavily wooded Burning Tree area of Bethesda, Maryland, for a man who escaped on foot and was described by police as armed and dangerous.

Officers responding to a home burglary alarm about 5:30 a.m. EST (1030 GMT) discovered a dark-coloured car travelling in the predawn darkness without lights. They gave chase and captured one man after the suspects stopped and fled on foot.

Police spokeswoman Ann Evans said the unnamed man was being interviewed and had not been charged with a crime. She could not confirm he was a suspect in the string of "British bandit" robberies in suburban Maryland since January.

Previous victims of the early morning robberies, all in the same area, described the two men as speaking with British or Australian accents. Police said they always demanded only cash and kept their faces covered.

"They demand cash. They don't want other valuables, all they want is cash. ... When they get the cash, they always leave by the way they came," Cpl. George Ludington said. He was not amused by the "British" nickname given the bandits in local news accounts. "We just call them criminals," he said.

The armed robberies began on Jan. 25 and the last one had been on Sunday morning. The first seven were at estates near Washington -- large homes with extensive grounds, often with security systems and guard dogs.

No injuries had been reported but Ludington said on Monday he feared that could change. "The groundwork's being set here for a real tragedy," he said. "We don't know what makes them tick ... the law of averages says that one of the homes they enter, the owner's going to be a gun owner and there could be a gun battle right there."
